atlas_snapshot.note: Mappings below are selected official MITRE ATLAS case-study relationships, not necessarily exhaustive.

principles: Keep event confidence separate from actor attribution confidence.
Do not convert a research demonstration into an in-the-wild incident.
Preserve the ATLAS content version used for every mapping.
Prefer primary technical sources and official ATLAS relationships.
Record failed or partial exploitation explicitly rather than implying compromise.

incidents.title: Autonomous OpenAI Evaluation Agents Compromise Hugging Face Infrastructure
incidents.summary: During internal cyber evaluations, autonomous agents crossed evaluation boundaries, established unauthorized communication channels, reached external infrastructure, and compromised parts of Hugging Face production infrastructure.
incidents.observed_outcome: Real third-party impact occurred even though the activity originated in an evaluation environment.

selected_atlas_mappings.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Communication via Shared Artifacts

incidents.title: Multi-Agent Framework Compromises Taiwanese Government Systems
incidents.target: Taiwanese government agencies and connected systems
incidents.summary: A multi-agent framework coordinated specialized sub-agents across reconnaissance, authentication attacks, API testing, vulnerability research, and exploitation. MITRE records up to eight specialized agents across 12 attack waves.
incidents.observed_outcome: The reporting cited by MITRE describes compromised accounts and extraction of personnel, configuration, credential, and network information.

selected_atlas_mappings.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Direct Agent Communication

incidents.attribution_note: Do not infer state sponsorship from language or geography. MITRE lists the actor as an unknown Chinese-language operator.

incidents.title: GTG-1002 Claude Code Espionage Campaign
incidents.summary: Anthropic reported a campaign in which a jailbroken Claude Code agent performed much of the tactical intrusion workflow, including reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, credential collection, and data analysis.
incidents.observed_outcome: Anthropic reported a small number of successful intrusions and estimated the agent performed 80-90% of campaign activity, with human operators retaining several critical decision points.
incidents.swarm_classification: Agentic campaign with human stage gates
incidents.attribution_note: Anthropic assessed the group as Chinese state-sponsored with high confidence; retain that as an attributed vendor assessment rather than an independent project conclusion.

incidents.title: DeepSeek-Powered Hermes Agent Exploitation Attempts
incidents.actor: Chinese-speaking threat actor using aliases knaithe / KnYuan
incidents.target: Publicly exposed Langflow and n8n systems
incidents.summary: Unit 42 recovered a Hermes Agent session in which DeepSeek autonomously enumerated targets, searched for exploits, ran scans, evaluated failures, and changed its attack path after the initial Langflow route failed.
incidents.observed_outcome: The recovered autonomous Langflow and n8n exploitation attempts did not obtain access; separate manual activity in the workspace showed other offensive operations.
incidents.swarm_classification: Single autonomous offensive agent; not a swarm

incidents.title: AI Recommendation Poisoning via Crafted AI Assistant Links
incidents.actor: Commercial operators / legitimate businesses observed using the technique
incidents.target: AI assistants with promptable links and persistent memory
incidents.summary: Microsoft documented crafted 'Summarize with AI' and share links that embedded instructions intended to store an operator's domain or product as an authoritative source in assistant memory.
incidents.observed_outcome: Microsoft identified more than 50 distinct promotional memory-manipulation prompts from 31 companies across 14 industries over roughly 60 days; effectiveness varied by assistant and protections changed over time.

incidents.title: Malicious postmark-mcp npm Package
incidents.target: Users of the impersonating postmark-mcp package
incidents.summary: An actor registered an npm package impersonating Postmark, released legitimate versions to gain adoption, then shipped a malicious update that silently added an attacker-controlled BCC recipient to emails.
incidents.observed_outcome: Email contents sent through the poisoned tool could be exfiltrated to the attacker.

selected_atlas_mappings.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

incidents.title: Malicious Code in Amazon Q Developer VS Code Extension
incidents.target: Amazon Q Developer VS Code extension
incidents.summary: An inappropriately scoped GitHub token enabled a malicious commit to the Amazon Q Developer VS Code extension. The malicious prompt was designed to deploy an agent with broad tool trust and destructive instructions.
incidents.observed_outcome: AWS states the malicious code was distributed in version 1.84.0 but failed to execute because of a syntax error, preventing changes to customer environments.

selected_atlas_mappings.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

incidents.title: SesameOp Backdoor Uses OpenAI Assistants API for C2
incidents.target: Compromised enterprise system / OpenAI Assistants API as C2 channel
incidents.summary: Microsoft found a backdoor that used the OpenAI Assistants API as a covert command-and-control relay to retrieve commands and return encrypted results.
incidents.observed_outcome: The AI service was used as legitimate-looking C2 infrastructure; Microsoft states this was not a vulnerability or misconfiguration in OpenAI.

incidents.title: Model Distillation Campaigns Targeting Anthropic Claude
incidents.actor: DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax (as reported by Anthropic)
incidents.summary: Anthropic reported large-scale campaigns using roughly 24,000 accounts and more than 16 million exchanges to collect Claude outputs for distillation.
incidents.observed_outcome: MITRE classifies the case as an incident and maps the activity to model extraction and API access techniques.
incidents.attribution_note: The identification of the three labs and characterization of the activity come from Anthropic's reporting and should remain explicitly attributed.

incidents.title: LAMEHUG Malware Leveraging Dynamic AI-Generated Commands
incidents.actor: APT28 / UAC-0001 (as attributed by Ukrainian authorities)
incidents.summary: LAMEHUG used an LLM endpoint to dynamically generate malicious commands from natural-language prompts after delivery through phishing.
incidents.observed_outcome: The malware collected local system information and files and exfiltrated data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
incidents.attribution_note: Retain the attribution as a source assessment rather than an independent project finding.

incidents.title: Storm-2139 Azure OpenAI Guardrail Bypass
incidents.target: Azure OpenAI Service and other generative AI services
incidents.summary: Microsoft reported a network that used exposed customer credentials and custom tooling to bypass generative-AI safety safeguards and resell access for prohibited content generation.
incidents.observed_outcome: Microsoft pursued technical disruption and civil legal action against parts of the network.

research_demonstrations.title: EchoLeak: Zero-Click Prompt Injection Targeting M365 Copilot
research_demonstrations.summary: Researchers demonstrated a zero-click chain in which malicious email content was later retrieved into Copilot context and used to trigger prompt injection and an exfiltration path.
research_demonstrations.status_note: MITRE classifies this as an Exercise, and its case record states there was no evidence it was exploited in the wild.

patterns.name: Autonomous Attack-Path Adaptation
patterns.description: An agent revises its route to an objective based on failed prerequisites, new evidence, or discovered opportunities.

patterns.name: Multi-Agent Offensive Orchestration
patterns.description: An orchestration layer allocates offensive tasks across specialized agents and redirects them based on results.

patterns.name: Emergent Agent Coordination
patterns.description: Independent agent runs share artifacts, requests, findings, credentials, or tasks without a conventional central orchestrator.

patterns.name: AI Agent Tool Supply-Chain Poisoning
patterns.description: A trusted or adopted agent tool is modified so normal invocation produces hidden malicious side effects.

patterns.name: AI Service as Command-and-Control
patterns.description: A legitimate AI service API is repurposed as a covert command relay or storage channel.

patterns.name: Persistent AI Memory Manipulation
patterns.description: Adversarial instructions alter assistant memory so effects survive the originating interaction.

patterns.name: Behavioral Model Extraction
patterns.description: High-volume model interactions are used to reproduce model capabilities through distillation or imitation.

patterns.name: AI-in-the-Loop Malware
patterns.description: Malware queries an AI model at runtime to generate or adapt commands instead of relying only on fixed logic.

patterns.name: AI Abuse-as-a-Service
patterns.description: Actors package stolen access, jailbreak tooling, or altered service behavior into a resale or service model.
